amanda (support): Hey team — escalating a customer 401 issue from AcmePayments. They started seeing intermittent 'invalid_signature' 401s after an IdP key rotation yesterday evening (~2024-11-02T22:10Z). I reproduced locally against their private deployment. Logs attached.

amanda (support): Logs show verifier failing with the customer's kid and our JWKS cache still pointing at older keys.
```
[2024-11-02T22:10:12Z] auth.verifier: signature verification failed, kid=abc123, error=signature_invalid
request_id=req_01E7FZ9XQ
jwt_header={"alg":"RS256","kid":"abc123"}
jwks_cache_hit=true, jwks_last_fetch=2024-11-01T18:02:00Z
```

amanda (support): Quick repro (from our env):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" https://private-api.redwood/acme/payments
# JWT header encoded -> {"alg":"RS256","kid":"abc123"}
```

amanda (support): When I decode the JWT I get `kid=abc123` which is NOT present in the JWKS we have cached for that tenant. The cached JWKS was last fetched ~28 hours ago. Customer says their IdP rotated keys ~22:00 UTC yesterday.

amanda (support): They also reported a small clock skew on their signing machines (ntp drift ~3s). Example token claims: `nbf` is 3s in future, `iat` same. Our verifier rejects tokens with >1s skew.

olga (eng-runtime): Thanks — this looks like two contributing factors: JWKS cache stale (long refresh interval) and tight clock tolerance. Our current JWKS refresh policy is 6h and we only refresh proactively; we do not refresh on `kid` mismatch.

olga (eng-runtime): Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) on verification failure due to UnknownKidError or signature mismatch, trigger an immediate JWKS refresh and retry verification once. 2) increase default clock tolerance to +/-5s for signed requests (configurable per-tenant). 3) add per-tenant cooldown for refresh-on-mismatch to avoid thundering herd (default 30s).

eve (eng-security): +1 to on-demand refresh. Important caveat: if an attacker can cause repeated mismatches, we must rate-limit refreshes. The per-tenant cooldown is good. Also document that extending clock tolerance increases replay risk; ensure we still enforce `jti`/nonce checks for high-value ops.

kevin (sre): We saw at least two nodes in eu-west with NTP issues last week (ntpd errors), so client-side skew is plausible. Will add monitoring for large clock jumps on the fleet. Also suggest a metric `auth.jwks_refresh_on_mismatch_total` and `auth.jwks_cache_hit_rate`.

ryan (customer): Confirmed from AcmePayments: their IdP rotates keys every 12–24h and they have a very short TTL. They asked whether the 6h cache could be shortened. They prefer minimal latency; will accept automatic refresh-on-mismatch if it doesn't slow down 99p latency.

olga (eng-runtime): Perf note: a refresh-on-mismatch is one HTTPS call to the IdP and one verification retry; on average ~30–80ms depending on IdP. We can make this async-blocking for the verification path (retry once synchronously) but fall back to a soft 401 with `www-authenticate: stale-key` header for clients that want to retry.

olga (eng-runtime): Proposed code change (pseudocode):
```python
# verifier.py
try:
    verified = verify(jwt, cached_jwks)
except UnknownKidError:
    if cooldown_expired(tenant):
        cached_jwks = fetch_jwks(tenant_jwks_url)
        verified = verify(jwt, cached_jwks)
    else:
        raise
```

olga (eng-runtime): Also, change time validation to `abs(now - claim_time) <= clock_tolerance_seconds` where default `clock_tolerance_seconds=5` (tenant-overridable).

amanda (support): Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate client-side changes. I sent them this curl to assert the kid mismatch and fetch live JWKS: 
```
curl -sS https://idp.acme.io/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'
# then decode token header
echo $JWT | cut -d'.' -f1 | base64 -d | jq
```

amanda (support): I also told them we will roll a hotfix that triggers JWKS refresh-on-mismatch and raise clock tolerance. ETA for canary: today CET afternoon.

kevin (sre): Suggest steps before canary: add the two metrics, add a short-lived feature flag `refresh_on_mismatch` (default off), and run 2% traffic for 1 hour then 10%. Add a dashboard showing `auth.failures.by_code` and `auth.jwks_refresh_attempts`.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: release/eng-runtime/jwks-refresh-fallback -> 2% traffic (canary id c-4421). :rocket:

amanda (support): Customer acknowledged and will watch for decrease in 401s. If this fixes it we'll propose defaulting refresh_on_mismatch to on for private deployments.

eve (eng-security): After canary, we should ship a short KB article for customers explaining: how key rotation should be done (publish JWKS ahead of rotation), recommended JWKS TTL, and guidance on NTP and clock tolerance.

olga (eng-runtime): I'll open the PR and link here. Action items: olga->PR w/ cooldown + retry logic, kevin->metrics + dashboard, eve->KB draft, amanda->customer communication.

amanda (support): Thanks — keeping thread open until customer confirms. :thumbsup:
